Andry Rajoelina (born 30 May 1974) is a politician and businessman who served as the eighth president of Madagascar from 2019 to 2025.

Astarte (Ancient) is the Hellenized form of the Ancient Near Eastern goddess Atart.

Benjamin was the younger of the two sons of Jacob and Rachel, and Jacob's twelfth and youngest son overall in Jewish, Christian and Islamic tradition.

The youngest of five sons in one of America's most famous banking dynasties, this economist and investment banker chaired Chase Manhattan Corporation and was renowned for his extensive foreign political connections — who is he?
David Rockefeller (June 12, 1915 - March 20, 2017) was an American economist and investment banker who served as chairman and chief executive of Chase Manhattan Corporation.
Son of a chambermaid and a carpenter, this British politician led the Conservatives, served as PM from 1970 to 1974, and was also a keen yachtsman and musician — who is he?
Edward Heath (9 July 1916 - 17 July 2005) was a British politician who served as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom from 1970 to 1974 and Leader of the Conservative Party from 1965 to 1975.

Galba (Latin; 24 December 3 BC - 15 January AD 69) was a Roman emperor, ruling for 7 months from 8 June AD 68 to 15 January 69.
A leader of the Nazi Party's northern faction whose talks with Chancellor von Schleicher in 1932 enraged Hitler, he was murdered in the Night of the Long Knives — who was he?
Gregor Strasser (31 May 1892 - 30 June 1934) was a German politician and early leader of the Nazi Party.
This German chancellor's 16-year tenure — the longest in the country's post-war history — spanned the end of the Cold War, German reunification, and the founding of the European Union — who is he?
Helmut Kohl (3 April 1930 - 16 June 2017) was a German politician who served as chancellor of Germany and governed the Federal Republic from 1982 to 1998.

Born a peasant in 1916 and working as a humble schoolmaster, this man slowly built such influence among the uneducated that he rose to lead Dahomey — today's Benin — into independence from France. Who was he?
Hubert Maga (August 10, 1916 - May 8, 2000) was a politician from Dahomey (now known as Benin).

A Confederate cavalry general famous for being Robert E. Lee's eyes and ears, he cultivated a cavalier image: red-lined gray cape, ostrich-plumed hat cocked to one side, and a splash of cologne. Who was this dashing horseman?
J. E. B. Stuart (February 6, 1833 - May 12, 1864) was a Confederate cavalry general during the American Civil War.

At just 16 years old, this Australian sailor circled the globe solo over seven months, though her southerly route technically fell short of the official distance for a true circumnavigation — who is she?
Jessica Watson (born 18 May 1993) is an Australian sailor who attempted a solo circumnavigation at the age of 16 from 18 October 2009 to 15 May 2010.
This Abrahamic, monotheistic faith is built on a body of tradition including the Torah and is regarded as one of the earliest monotheistic religions — which religion is this?
Judaism is an Abrahamic, monotheistic, ethnic religion that comprises the collective spiritual, cultural, and legal traditions of the Jewish people.
This royal dependency's parliament was dominated by the Protestant Anglo-Irish Ascendancy, and its status as a subordinate realm was enshrined by the Declaratory Act of 1719 — what was it called?
Kingdom of Ireland was a dependency of England from 1542 to 1707, and then of Great Britain from 1707 to 1800.
Dubbed the 'Oriental Bismarck' for being the face of the Qing court abroad, this late-Qing statesman founded the Huai Army and the Beiyang Fleet and led the Self-Strengthening Movement. Who is he?
Li Hongzhang (also Li Hung-chang; February 15, 1823 - November 7, 1901) was a Chinese statesman of the late Qing dynasty.

Founded in 1932 on land seized in Japan's invasion of Manchuria and recognized mostly by Axis-aligned states, this short-lived puppet 'monarchy' was widely regarded as illegitimate — what was it called?
Manchukuo was a puppet state of the Empire of Japan in Manchuria that existed from 1932 until its dissolution in 1945.
This American memoirist and poet's first of seven autobiographies, published in 1969, told of her life up to age 17 and brought her international recognition. Who is she?
Maya Angelou (born Marguerite Annie Johnson; April 4, 1928 - May 28, 2014) was an American memoirist, essayist, poet, and civil rights activist.

Commanding both the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and the Muslim Peshmerga during the Iran-Iraq War, this Iranian officer, who died in 1983, helped restore Iran's control over Kurdistan — who was he?
Mohammad Boroujerdi (1955 - 1983) was an Iranian commander in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps during the Iran-Iraq War.
Having fought in the Civil War, the last Indian Wars, and the Spanish-American War, this officer served from 1895 to 1903 as the very last Commanding General of the U.S. Army — who was he?

Nelson A. Miles (August 8, 1839 - May 15, 1925) was a United States Army officer who served in the American Civil War (1861-1865), the last stages of the American Indian Wars (1840-1890), and the Spanish-American War (1898).
Meaning roughly 'salutations to the auspicious one,' this five-syllable Hindu mantra is the most important in Shaivism and is dedicated to Lord Shiva — what is it?

Considered the most influential artist of the Flemish Baroque tradition, this painter and diplomat's dramatic, sensual style of movement and color helped define Counter-Reformation art — who is he?
Peter Paul Rubens (28 June 1577 - 30 May 1640) was a Flemish artist and diplomat.
Built on the belief that inherited attributes make one group superior to another, this term also covers everyday prejudice against people of a different ethnic background. What is it?
Racism is the belief that groups of humans possess different behavioral traits corresponding to inherited attributes and can be divided based on the superiority of one race or ethnicity over another.

Robert Muldoon (25 September 1921 - 5 August 1992) was a New Zealand politician who served as the 31st prime minister of New Zealand, from 1975 to 1984, while leader of the National Party.
She led Finland's Social Democrats from 2020 to 2023 and was the country's prime minister before resigning her parliament seat to advise political leaders abroad — who is she?

Sanna Marin (born 16 November 1985) is a Finnish politician who served as prime minister of Finland from 2019 to 2023 and as the leader of the Social Democratic Party of Finland (SDP) from 2020 to 2023.
This mythical king of Corinth angered Zeus by revealing one of his affairs, and was punished in the underworld by eternally pushing a boulder up a hill only to watch it roll back down — name him?
Sisyphus (Ancient) is the founder and king of Ephyra (now known as Corinth).

This ancient Chinese philosophical and religious tradition emphasizes harmony with an all-encompassing 'Way' running through nature, informing practices like meditation, feng shui, and internal alchemy — name this tradition?
Taoism is a philosophical and religious tradition indigenous to China, emphasizing harmony with the Tao.

Ahmed I: Sultan of the Ottoman Empire from 1603 to 1617.

Fall of Kabul (2021): Taliban capture of the capital of Afghanistan.

Francisco Macías Nguema: President of Equatorial Guinea from 1968 to 1979.

Gauls: Ancient Celtic peoples of Europe.

Gog and Magog: Pair of individuals, peoples, or lands in the Bible and the Quran.
A key player in the 1963 Ba'athist coup, this Syrian officer ruled as president from 1971 until his death in 2000 — and passed power to his son. Who was he?

Tutankhamun: Pharaoh of Egypt from 1333 to 1324 BC.
Named for a queen who reigned from 1837 until 1901, this period saw the Irish Famine and the Crimean War against Russia — what was it called?
Victorian era: Queen Victoria's reign, 1837 to 1901.

In 1806, fearing Napoleon's growing power after the Confederation of the Rhine formed, Prussia joined Russia, Saxony, Sweden and Britain in a fresh multinational stand against the French Empire — which conflict?
War of the Fourth Coalition: 1806–1807 conflict of the Napoleonic Wars.
Commander of the Indonesian Armed Forces during the country's 1998 transition from authoritarian rule, this retired general later chaired the Presidential Advisory Council — who is it?
Wiranto: Indonesian general and politician. On 27 July 2016, Wiranto was appointed Coordinating Minister for Political, Legal, and Security Affairs, replacing Luhut Binsar Panjaitan.
Serving as Japan's foreign minister from 2023 to 2024, she previously held the justice portfolio and worked on gender-equality policy under two different prime ministers — who is she?
Which of these four is the eldest?
Eratosthenes (born 276 BC) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these people was born first?
Qian Xuesen (born 1911) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four is the eldest?
Henry Vaughan (born 1621) is the earliest of the four. Henry Vaughan (1621 – 23 April 1695) was a Welsh metaphysical poet, author and translator writing in English, and a medical physician.
COBOL (founded 1959) is the earliest of the four.
Which of these four appeared first?
Lisp (programming language) (published 1958) is the earliest of the four.
Pick the physicist from these four.
Mark Oliphant is a physicist. Born and raised in Adelaide, South Australia, Oliphant graduated from the University of Adelaide in 1922.
Who among these is a chemist?
Carolyn Bertozzi is a chemist. Carolyn Ruth Bertozzi (born October 10, 1966) is an American chemist and Nobel laureate, known for her wide-ranging work spanning both chemistry and biology.
What is the atomic number of Fluorine?
Fluorine is a chemical element; it has symbol F and atomic number 9.
In what year was Hedy Lamarr born?
Hedy Lamarr (born Hedwig Eva Maria Kiesler; November 9, 1914 – January 19, 2000) was an Austrian and American actress and inventor.
In what year was Acupuncture discovered?
Acupuncture is a form of alternative medicine and a component of traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) in which thin needles are inserted into the body.
In what year was SARS-CoV-2 discovered?
SARS-CoV-2: The virus previously had the provisional name 2019 novel coronavirus (2019-nCoV), and has also been called human coronavirus 2019 (HCoV-19 or hCoV-19).
Furosemide: Pfizer. Furosemide, sold under the brand name Lasix among others, is a loop diuretic medication used to treat edema due to heart failure, liver scarring, or kidney disease.
LIGO: United States. The Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory (LIGO) is a large-scale physics experiment and observatory designed to detect cosmic gravitational waves.
Who is credited with discovering Cadmium?
Cadmium: Friedrich Stromeyer. Cadmium is a chemical element; it has symbol Cd and atomic number 48.
Who is credited with discovering Pigeonhole principle?

Pigeonhole principle: Johann Peter Gustav Lejeune Dirichlet. In mathematics, the pigeonhole principle states that if n items are put into m containers, with n > m, then at least one container must contain more than one item.
Who is credited with discovering Galactic Center?
Galactic Center: Harlow Shapley. The Galactic Center is the barycenter of the Milky Way and a corresponding point on the rotational axis of the galaxy.
First unearthed in Montana in 1987 by a team led by Jack Horner, this horned dinosaur genus takes its name from a Greek river deity — name the genus?
Achelousaurus is a genus of centrosaurine ceratopsid dinosaur that lived during the Late Cretaceous Period of what is now North America, about 77 to 74.8 million years ago.
The twelfth-brightest star in our night sky and the brightest in the constellation Aquila. It's one of the three vertices of the Summer Triangle asterism. Name this star.

Altair is the brightest star in the equatorial constellation of Aquila and the twelfth-brightest star in the night sky. It has the Bayer designation Alpha Aquilae, which is Latinised from α Aquilae and abbreviated Alpha Aql or α Aql.
What term describes the discipline of measuring human body dimensions, applied everywhere from ergonomics and architecture to tracking historical living standards?
Anthropometry (from Ancient Greek (nthrpos) 'human' and (mtron) 'measure') refers to the measurement of the human individual.

It's one of the oldest natural sciences, recruiting math, physics, and chemistry to explain everything that originates beyond Earth's atmosphere — from comets and quasars to the cosmic microwave background. What field is it?
Astronomy is a natural science that studies celestial objects and the phenomena that occur in the cosmos.
This steel-gray, lightweight metal with atomic number 4 is found in gemstones like aquamarine and emerald, but within the cores of stars it gets destroyed as fast as it forms — what element is it?
Beryllium is a chemical element; it has symbol Be and atomic number 4.
This incurable, always-fatal disease of cattle causes abnormal behavior and trouble walking, with symptoms that may take four to five years to appear after infection — what is this disorder called?
Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE), commonly known as mad cow disease, is an incurable and always fatal neurodegenerative disease of cattle.

One species in this genus of flowering shrubs, native to southern China and Indochina, has its leaves processed into the world's tea, while thousands of ornamental cultivars exist for the garden. Name the genus?
Camellia is a genus of flowering plants in the family Theaceae.
A secondarily aquatic clade within the order that also includes hippos, this infraorder covers whales, dolphins and porpoises, along with extinct relatives like Basilosaurus — which group of animals?

Cetacean are marine mammals belonging to the infraorder Cetacea, a secondarily aquatic clade under the order Artiodactyla that include whales, dolphins, porpoises and extinct groups such as Basilosaurus.
This tangor — a mandarin-orange cross — typically splits into seven to fourteen easy-to-peel segments — which fruit?
Clementine (Citrus clementina) is a tangor, a citrus fruit hybrid between a willowleaf mandarin orange (C. deliciosa) and a sweet orange (C. sinensis).
Made up of subregions called the genu, rostrum, trunk, and splenium, this thick nerve tract lets the brain's two hemispheres communicate — what is it?
Corpus callosum (Latin for "tough body"), also callosal commissure, is a wide, thick nerve tract, consisting of a flat bundle of commissural fibers, beneath the cerebral cortex in the brain.
In psychiatry, this is a fixed belief that persists even in the face of clear and obvious evidence to the contrary, distinguishing it from a merely mistaken or strongly held idea — what is it called?
Delusion is a fixed belief that is not amenable to change in light of conflicting evidence.

Defined in humans as an adult height of 147 centimeters or less, this condition can be disproportionate (affecting limbs or torso alone) or proportionate, and typically comes with normal intelligence and near-normal life expectancy — which condition?
Dwarfism is a condition of people and animals marked by unusually small size or short stature.
Built from flattened cells atop a columnar basal layer, this outer skin barrier regulates water loss and grows thinner as a person ages — what is it?
Epidermis is the outermost of the three major layers that constitute the skin, the inner layers being the dermis and hypodermis.
This type of anaerobic metabolism harnesses the redox potential of reactants like glucose to produce ATP without needing oxygen. What process is it?
Fermentation is a type of anaerobic metabolism that harnesses the redox potential of the reactants to make adenosine triphosphate (ATP) and organic end products.
Son of a wealthy Greek architect, this 2nd-century physician and philosopher's writings shaped anatomy, physiology, pharmacology, and neurology for centuries after his death — who is he?
Credited alongside Isaac Newton with inventing calculus, this German polymath also pioneered binary arithmetic and has been called the 'last universal genius' — who is he?
Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz was German polymath (1646–1716).

One of the first plants ever spun into fiber some 50,000 years ago, which fast-growing Cannabis sativa cultivar is grown for rope, textiles, paper, biofuel and food rather than its psychoactive punch?
Hemp is a plant in the botanical class of Cannabis sativa cultivars grown specifically for industrial and consumable use.

This large insect order includes sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants, with more than 150,000 described species, many of whose females have an egg-laying organ often modified into a stinger — what is it called?
Hymenoptera is a large order of insects, comprising the sawflies, wasps, bees, and ants.
This mild oxidizing agent and Lewis acid, with the formula FeCl3, is commonly used to purify water and to etch metal surfaces — which compound is it?
Iron(III) chloride is an inorganic compound with the formula FeCl3. The anhydrous derivative is a Lewis acid, while all forms are mild oxidizing agents.

A civil engineer who commanded the Australian Corps in 1918, this WWI general was called by historian A. J. P. Taylor 'the only general of creative originality produced by the First World War' — who was he?
John Monash (27 June 1865 - 8 October 1931) was an Australian military commander of the First World War and a civil engineer.
When the natural curve of the thoracic spine exceeds about 45 degrees, doctors give this excessive rounding of the upper back a name rooted in the Greek word for 'hump' — what is it?
Kyphosis (from Greek (kyphos) 'hump') is an abnormally excessive convex curvature of the spine as it occurs in the thoracic and sacral regions.
Born in 1880, this Australian therapist and part-time stage actor is remembered for coaching a stammering British monarch — who is he?
Lionel Logue (26 February 1880 - 12 April 1953) was an Australian speech and language therapist and amateur stage actor who helped King George VI manage his stammer.

An engineer and teacher from a poor family who once served as mayor of Tehran, this politician became Iran's sixth president in 2005 and was a fierce proponent of the country's nuclear program — who is he?
Mahmoud Ahmadinejad (n Sabbaghian; born 28 October 1956) is an Iranian politician who served as the sixth president of Iran from 2005 to 2013.
Driven by hormones, this coordinated pair of bodily rhythms — one governing the ovaries, the other the uterine lining — usually runs 21 to 35 days and begins around age 12. What is it called?
Menstrual cycle is a series of natural changes in hormone production and the structures of the uterus and ovaries of the female reproductive system that makes pregnancy possible.
Named from a Greek word for lead because its ores were once confused with lead ore, this chemical element bears the symbol Mo and atomic number 42 — name the element?
Molybdenum is a chemical element; it has symbol Mo and atomic number 42.

What term, coined in the mid-19th century and often attributed to pathologist Rudolf Virchow, describes the premature death of cells in living tissue due to external injury or infection, as opposed to programmed cell death?
Necrosis (from Ancient Greek (nkrsis) 'death') is a form of cell injury which results in the premature death of cells in living tissue by autolysis.
Named after a German physicist, this SI unit of electrical resistance is represented by the uppercase Greek letter omega — name the unit?
Ohm (symbol:, the uppercase Greek letter omega) is the unit of electrical resistance in the International System of Units (SI).

This skin sensation — often described as tingling, prickling, or numbness — is most familiar as the 'pins and needles' feeling after a limb falls asleep from staying still too long — name this sensation?
Paresthesia (or paraesthesia) is a sensation of the skin that may feel like numbness (hypoesthesia), tingling, pricking, chilling, or burning.
Colorless in acid and a vivid pink in base, which phthalein dye is the chemist's go-to indicator for acid-base titrations?
Phenolphthalein (feh-NOL(F)-th-leen) is a chemical compound with the formula C20H14O4 and is often written as "HIn", "HPh", "phph" or simply "Ph" in shorthand notation.

This academic field studies systems of governance and power, favoring descriptive and empirical analysis of behavior and institutions over the value judgments used in philosophy about the state — name the discipline?
Political science (sometimes abbreviated as poli sci) is a field which aims to study the scientific aspect of politics.
Split into roughly a dozen Afrotropical species and around 167 Neotropical species — among them the blue-and-yellow macaw and the grey parrot — which bird family is this?
Psittacidae is one of three families of true parrots.
What dimensionless quantity in fluid dynamics, expressing the ratio of inertial to viscous forces, determines whether a flow will be smooth and laminar or chaotic and turbulent?
Reynolds number (Re) is a dimensionless quantity that helps predict fluid flow patterns in different situations by measuring the ratio between inertial and viscous forces.
Named after an American veterinary surgeon, this genus of rod-shaped, gram-negative bacteria includes over 2,650 serotypes within a single major species — name it?
Salmonella is a genus of rod-shaped, (bacillus) Gram-negative bacteria of the family Enterobacteriaceae.
This Pakistani-American businessman owns both an NFL franchise, the Jacksonville Jaguars, and an English Premier League club, Fulham — who is he?
Shahid Khan (born July 18, 1950) is a Pakistani and American businessman.
Beginning with stem cells near the basement membrane and passing through two rounds of meiosis, this process turns germ cells into haploid sperm inside the seminiferous tubules — what is it called?
Spermatogenesis is the process by which haploid spermatozoa develop from germ cells in the seminiferous tubules of the testicle.

Practiced by professionals who determine property boundaries and construction points using total stations, GNSS receivers, and lidar sensors, which technical discipline combines geometry, trigonometry, and law?
Surveying is the technique, profession, art, and science of determining the terrestrial positions of points based on the distances and angles between them.
This part of the lower limb sits between the hip and the knee, containing a single thick bone — the femur — that forms a ball-and-socket joint above and a hinge joint below — name the body part?
Thigh is the area between the hip (pelvis) and the knee.
Several highly prized truffle species belong to this fungal genus, whose lineage is estimated to date to the close of the Jurassic period — which genus?
Tuber (fungus) is a genus in the fungal family Tuberaceae, with estimated molecular dating to the end of the Jurassic period (156 Mya).
This Russian-American inventor built a television system using cathode-ray tubes and worked on image tubes and the electron microscope — who was he?
Vladimir K. Zworykin (1888/1889 - July 29, 1982) was a Russian-American inventor, engineer, and pioneer of television technology.
Which East Asian citrus fruit, believed to have originated in central China as a hybrid of mandarin orange and ichang papeda, is now also grown in New Zealand, Australia, and parts of Europe?
Yuzu (Citrus junos, from Japanese or) is a citrus fruit and plant in the family Rutaceae of Chinese origin.
Native to Africa and Yemen, this drought-resistant tree species has individuals radiocarbon-dated to over 1,275 years old — what is it?
Adansonia digitata: Species of plant native to Africa.
Brother of a concert pianist and son of an astronomer, this Russian mathematician built the foundational theory of stability in dynamical systems — who was he?
Formed when ammonia gains an extra hydrogen ion, this positively charged molecule, NH4+, is a key player in the global nitrogen cycle — what is it?
Bridging biology and sociology, this scientific study of humanity has social, cultural, linguistic and biological branches, and treats archaeology as the study of the human past — what's the field?
Anthropology: Scientific study of humans, human behavior, and societies.
Unlike its counterpart which returns blood to the heart, this blood vessel usually carries oxygen-rich blood away from it — what is it?
Artery: Blood vessels that carry blood away from the heart.
Best known for pioneering radical behaviorism at Harvard, this psychologist invented a chamber for studying operant conditioning that came to bear his name — who is he?
B. F. Skinner: American psychologist and social philosopher (1904–1990)
Originating in the Swiss Alps' canton of Bern, this large farm breed historically pulled carts for alpine herders and traces its ancestry to Roman mastiffs — which breed, recognized in 1912?
Bernese Mountain Dog: Swiss breed of dog. The Bernese Mountain Dog, German: Berner Sennenhund or Dürrbächler, is a large dog breed originating from the canton of Bern, Switzerland and the Swiss Alps.
The only trijet ever produced by its manufacturer, this airliner entered service with Eastern Air Lines in 1964 powered by three rear-mounted turbofans?
Ranging from roughly seawater-strength up to a fully saturated 26%, which salty solution is used for pickling food, de-icing roads, and turns up as a wastewater byproduct of desalination?
Brine: Concentrated solution of salt in water.
Named to honor the Virgin Mary and her golden crown, this daisy-family flower is also known as the pot marigold — which plant?
Calendula officinalis: Species of flowering plant in the daisy family Asteraceae.
Known also as yoke elm, this species of hornbeam native to Western Asia and Europe grows only up to elevations of about 1,000 metres — which species?
Carpinus betulus: Species of tree. It requires a warm climate for good growth, and occurs only at elevations up to 1,000 metres (3,300 ft).
Often called 'the father of the computer,' this English polymath designed the difference engine and the analytical engine, borrowing a punch-card principle from the Jacquard loom — who is he?
Charles Babbage: English mathematician, philosopher, and engineer (1791–1871)
One of the original citrus fruits, this large fragrant relative of the lemon has a thick, coarse rind and is a genetic ancestor of most modern citrus hybrids — what is it?

This medium-sized bird of prey ranges across Europe into northwestern China, hunting rodents like voles from a perch, with northern populations migrating as far as South Africa for winter — what bird is this?
Common buzzard: Species of bird of prey. It is a member of the genus Buteo in the family Accipitridae.
Spread mainly through the fecal-oral route, these single-stranded RNA enteroviruses share traits with poliovirus and rank among the leading causes of aseptic meningitis — which pathogens?
Coxsackievirus: Virus that causes digestive upset and sometimes heart damage.
This Harvard-trained legal scholar who wrote on criminal punishment and retribution joined Florida State's faculty in 2005, and was later murdered in a plot tied to his ex-wife's family — who is he?
Dan Markel: American law professor and murder victim (1972–2014)
This colorless, highly flammable liquid with a sweet smell was once widely used as a general anesthetic before modern alternatives — what compound?
After co-founding a social media giant, this entrepreneur left in 2008 to launch the workplace software company Asana — who is he?
Nicknamed the ALX, this Brazilian turboprop light-attack aircraft is assembled in Jacksonville, Florida with an American defense partner for low-threat counter-insurgency missions — which aircraft?
Embraer EMB 314 Super Tucano: Light ground attack and training aircraft.
Odorless, colorless, and dangerously sweet-tasting, this viscous compound goes into polyester fibers and antifreeze — and has even been spotted in outer space. What is it?
Born in 1963, this woman is the daughter of the last Shah of Iran by his third wife — who is she?
The lightest halogen, this pale yellow gas is so reactive that several 19th-century chemists died or were injured trying to isolate it, until Henri Moissan finally succeeded in 1886 — which element?
Fluorine: Chemical element with atomic number 9 (F)
Born in Pisa in 1564, this Italian polymath has been crowned the father of observational astronomy and the scientific method — and was among the earliest tinkerers to build a thermoscope. Who is he?
Galileo Galilei: Italian physicist and astronomer (1564–1642)

This Italian friar and cosmological theorist proposed that stars were distant suns with their own planets, and was tried for heresy by the Roman Inquisition for insisting the universe is infinite — who was he?
Giordano Bruno: Italian Dominican friar, philosopher and mathematician (1548–1600)
Unlike its rocky, mountain-dwelling marmot relatives, this solitary lowland rodent — also called the woodchuck — is common across the Eastern U.S., Canada, and Alaska. What is it?
Groundhog: Species of rodent. The groundhog (Marmota monax), also known as the woodchuck, is a rodent of the family Sciuridae, belonging to the group of large ground squirrels known as marmots.

Often defined as the normal functioning of the body free of disease, pain, or injury, this multidimensional state of well-being can be promoted by exercise and sleep and harmed by smoking or stress — what's the one-word concept?
Health: Desirable level of functional or metabolic efficiency of a living being.
Also called urticaria, this skin condition brings red or flesh-colored raised, itchy bumps that may sting and often follow an allergic reaction — what is it?
Hives: Skin disease characterized by red, raised, and itchy bumps.
Named from Greek words meaning "over" and "formation," this condition enlarges tissue by increasing the number of cells rather than their size — which term, distinct from hypertrophy?
Hyperplasia: Enlargement of tissue due to cell proliferation.
Commonly known as chaga, this parasitic fungus grows on birch trees and forms a charcoal-like black mass often marketed, questionably, as a health supplement — what's its scientific name?
Inonotus obliquus: Species of fungus. Inonotus obliquus, commonly called chaga (a Latinization of the Russian word ча́га), is a fungus in the family Hymenochaetaceae.
The first woman to chair the Federal Reserve, this American economist later became the first woman to serve as U.S. Treasury secretary — who is she?
Janet Yellen: American economist and government official (born 1946)
Named the type genus of the walnut family, this group of deciduous trees produces the walnuts eaten worldwide, with China responsible for half the global supply — which genus?
Juglans: Genus of trees. Walnut trees are any species of tree in the plant genus Juglans, the type genus of the family Juglandaceae, the seeds of which are referred to as walnuts.
Caused by a thiamine deficiency often linked to heavy alcohol use, this brain disorder is marked by amnesia and confabulation, and frequently pairs with Wernicke encephalopathy — which condition?
Korsakoff syndrome: Mental illness caused by a lack of thiamine in the brain.
Also called Hansen's disease, this slow bacterial infection dulls the body's sense of pain so badly that unnoticed injuries can cost a person their fingers and toes — what is it?
Leprosy: Chronic disease caused by bacterial infection.
Born as a Skunk Works black project and nicknamed "Habu," this Mach 3+ reconnaissance aircraft carried a crew of two in tandem cockpits — which plane is it?
Lockheed SR-71 Blackbird: US Air Force supersonic aircraft, 1964–1998.
First named in 1703 to honor a French botanist, this genus of 200-plus flowering trees and shrubs produces large fragrant blooms and cone-like autumn fruits — which genus?
Magnolia: Genus of angiosperms. Magnolia is a large genus of about 210 to 340 flowering plant species in the subfamily Magnolioideae of the family Magnoliaceae.
Born in Erfurt in 1864, this German jurist-turned-scholar became one of the founding figures of sociology before a breakdown following his father's death halted his teaching — who was he?
Max Weber: German sociologist, jurist, and political economist (1864–1920)
This field studies how we study — analyzing, comparing, and evaluating the procedures researchers use to gather and interpret data, shaped by underlying philosophical assumptions. What is it called?
Native to Southeast Asia, this evergreen tree's leaves are known as kratom, containing alkaloids that bind to opioid receptors — which species?
Mitragyna speciosa: Species of plant. It is under preliminary research for possible antipsychotic and antidepressant properties.

Named for being quieter than its relatives, this large white waterfowl carries an orange beak topped with a black knob that's bigger in males, and is more common in North America than in its native Europe — which bird?
Mute swan: Large species of waterfowl. The mute swan (Cygnus olor) is a species of swan and a member of the family Anatidae within the waterfowl order.
Also known in everyday speech as 'brain surgery,' this medical specialty treats disorders of the brain, spinal cord, and the entire nervous system — what is it called?
Neurosurgery: Medical specialty of disorders which affect any portion of the nervous system.
Thriving in the cool, wet summers of Northwest Europe, this hardy cereal grass tolerates low-nutrient, acidic soil and is dominated globally by Canadian and Russian production?
Derived from an ancient Roman unit called the uncia, this measure comes in an avoirdupois version equal to 1/16 of a pound and a heavier troy version used for precious metals — what unit is it?
Ounce: Unit of mass. The ounce is any of several different units of mass, weight, or volume and is derived almost unchanged from the uncia, an Ancient Roman unit of measurement.
Also called androgenetic alopecia, this condition driven by male sex hormones and genetics shows up as a receding hairline or a thinning crown in men — what's the common name for it?
Pattern hair loss: Medical condition. Pattern hair loss, also known as androgenetic alopecia, is a hair loss condition that primarily affects the top and front of the scalp.
Structurally related to a calming brain chemical and acting like baclofen or GHB on the same receptor, this anxiety medication can also give a mild dopamine-driven lift at low doses — what is it?
Caused by HPV and appearing on the sole of the foot with tiny black dots visible on its surface, this painful skin growth is treated with salicylic acid or freezing — what condition is it?
Plantar wart: Medical condition. A plantar wart, also known as a verruca, is a wart occurring on the bottom of the foot or toes.
Diagnosed only when symptoms like bloating, mood swings, and irritability disrupt daily life in the week or two before a period and resolve once it begins — what's this condition called?
Premenstrual syndrome: Emotional and physical symptoms that occur one to two weeks before a menstrual period.
This white-yellow-brown fluid forms at sites of infection, and when trapped in an enclosed tissue space, it creates what's known as an abscess — what is it called?
Pus: Fluid produced by inflammatory infection.

Named after a 19th-century British naturalist employed by the East India Company, this small deer species native to south-eastern China and Taiwan has also become an established wild population in the UK and Ireland — what is it?
Reeves's muntjac: Species of deer. It has also been introduced in the United Kingdom, Ireland, the Netherlands, Belgium, and Japan.
Grown in South Africa's Fynbos biome, this caffeine-free herbal infusion has an earthy flavor similar to yerba mate and carries protected designation of origin status in the EU. What is it?
Rooibos: Species of plant in the family Fabaceae.

This Harvard political scientist coordinated security planning for Jimmy Carter's National Security Council, but he's best remembered for a 1993 theory arguing future wars would be fought between cultures rather than countries — who was he?
Samuel P. Huntington: American political scientist and academic (1927–2008)

Nicknamed the 'last Soviet citizen' for being aboard Mir when the USSR dissolved, this cosmonaut flew six missions and helped connect the first Russian and American modules of a space station — who is he?
Sergei Krikalev: Soviet and Russian cosmonaut (born 1958)
Sometimes triggered just by stepping into bright sunlight, a quirk called the photic reflex, this involuntary, explosive expulsion of air clears irritants from the nose and mouth. What is it?
Sneeze: Semi-autonomous, convulsive expulsion of air from the lungs through the nose and mouth.

Named after the patron saint of sailors, this luminous blue or violet glow appears around masts, spires, or aircraft during a strong electric field and can warn of an imminent lightning strike — what is this phenomenon called?
St. Elmo's fire: Luminous plasma created in an electric field.
This medical specialty uses manual and instrumental techniques to treat disease, reshape the body, or remove diseased tissue, performed by a lead practitioner and an assistant?
Surgery: Medical procedures that involve incisive or invasive instruments into body cavities.

Named after the Latin word for 'earth' despite being one of the rarest elements in Earth's crust, this brittle silver-white metalloid with atomic number 52 was first found in a Transylvanian gold mine — what is it?
Tellurium: Chemical element with atomic number 52 (Te)

Spread by the bite of certain infected arachnids, this viral illness of the central nervous system can cause meningitis and lasting cognitive problems, with cases up nearly 400% across Europe in three decades — what is it?

Tick-borne encephalitis: Viral infection of the nervous system. Tick-borne encephalitis (TBE) is a viral infectious disease involving the central nervous system, transmitted by the bite of several species of infected ticks.

This genetic disorder causes small body size, heart defects, clenched fists with overlapping fingers, and severe intellectual disability, with risk rising alongside maternal age. What's the condition?
Trisomy 18: Chromosomal disorder in which there are three copies of chromosome 18.
Native to Europe and southwestern Asia, this herbaceous perennial is the type species that lends its name to an entire genus of flowering plants — what is it?
Valerian (herb): Species of flowering plant. Valerian (Valeriana officinalis) is an herbaceous perennial flowering plant in the family Caprifoliaceae, native to Europe and southwestern Asia.
Denoted by the Greek letter lambda, this measure of a repeating wave's spatial period shrinks as frequency rises for a wave moving at constant speed — what is it called?
Wavelength: Distance over which a wave's shape repeats.
Spread mainly by the oriental rat flea, this gram-negative bacterium caused the Black Death and the Plague of Justinian — what is it?
Yersinia pestis: Species of bacteria, cause of plague.

The symbol for livermorium is Lv. Livermorium is a synthetic chemical element; it has symbol Lv and atomic number 116.
